landmarks.name: Kumsusan Palace of the Sun
landmarks.writeup: The mausoleum where the bodies of Kim Il-sung and Kim Jong-il lie in state, serving as a significant political and cultural site.

landmarks.name: Juche Tower
landmarks.writeup: A monument symbolizing the Juche ideology, located in Pyongyang, representing self-reliance.

landmarks.name: Mount Paektu
landmarks.writeup: A sacred volcanic mountain considered the mythical birthplace of the Korean people and important in North Korean propaganda.

landmarks.name: Arch of Triumph
landmarks.writeup: Built to commemorate Korean resistance to Japan from 1925 to 1945, it is one of the largest triumphal arches in the world.

landmarks.name: Mansudae Grand Monument
landmarks.writeup: Features large statues of Kim Il-sung and Kim Jong-il, a central site for public homage.

cultural_events.name: Mass Games
cultural_events.writeup: A large-scale gymnastics and artistic festival showcasing synchronized performances that promote state ideology.

cultural_events.name: Day of the Sun
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrates the birth of Kim Il-sung on April 15, marked by parades and cultural performances.

cultural_events.name: Arirang Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A mass gymnastics and artistic festival held in Pyongyang, emphasizing unity and patriotism.

food_writeup: North Korean cuisine features staples like kimchi, cold noodles (naengmyeon), and rice dishes, often characterized by simple, hearty flavors with an emphasis on locally available ingredients.
brief_history: Established in 1948 following the division of Korea after World War II, North Korea developed as a socialist state under Kim Il-sung. It has since been ruled by the Kim dynasty, maintaining a strict centralized government and isolationist policies.
current_conflicts: Ongoing tensions with South Korea and the international community over North Korea's nuclear weapons program and human rights issues.
